418.t: When bands had one trombone and the section grew
418.s: Early bands had one trumpet and a trombone, then two trumpets and a trombone, and the trombone part was usually written out.
418.ch: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
418.q: No. A lot of times it was written out. If they had arrangements. Yeah, it was probably written out. Because if you had to play the trumpet you had to play it out. They always used to have just two trumpets and a trombone.

418.t: When bands had one trombone and the section grew
418.s: Early bands had one trumpet and a trombone, then two trumpets and a trombone, and the trombone part was usually written out.
418.ch: Trombone technique, plunger mute and the California years
418.q: No, a lot of the times it was written out. It was written out if they had arrangements. Yeah, it was probably written out, because you had to play with the trumpet. You had to play... They only used to have just two

418.t: When bands had one trombone and the section grew
418.s: Early bands had one trumpet and a trombone, then two trumpets and a trombone, and the trombone part was usually written out.
418.ch: Technique and life on the road (repeated passages)
418.q: No. A lot of times it was written out. If they had arrangements. Yeah, it was probably written out. Because if you had to play the trumpet you had to play itout. They always used to have just two trumpets and a trombone.

634.t: Band instrumentation: no piano, Tink, trombone
634.s: The band had no regular piano; they hired different players, often Tink. It had a trombone but no violin.
634.q: Page 5. Did you use a piano in the band? No, there wasn't any piano. Only when we get a job where the piano was, it was either high. It's different piano players. No.

634.t: Tulane band personnel and brass-band instrumentation
634.s: Members of the Tulane band, and how brass bands of that era used E-flat and alto horns, baritone and bass, in eleven pieces.
634.ch: Tulane Brass Band and bass drum
634.q: Tones and all that. Mm-hmm. Those bands, those days had, had what a brass band called for. Mm-hmm. It didn't look like none of the other goes, you're more on the E-flat or saxophone. And the tenor saxophone, then the golfers have got a band. But those days, they had that great big heavy artillery.…

127.t: Raceland band members and who played which instrument
127.s: Miller names the roughly eighteen members of the Raceland band and assigns instruments for the interviewer's list.
127.q: Well they had about four trombones, two baritones, two tubas, three altos, and they had two snare drum players, one bass drum. They didn't have no saxophones, and oh that's right, they had two clarinets, but they didn't have no saxophone.

127.s: Punch explains bands then had no saxophone and rarely piano: clarinet, trumpet, banjo, bass and drums.
127.ch: Jack Carey's band and piano players
127.q: Five pieces. Clarinet, trumpet, banjo, bass, and drum. That's what the band didn't do in time. Full band.

173.t: Size and instrumentation of the American Brass Band
173.s: Ten to twelve men, always three cornets, sometimes clarinet; B flat cornets preferred over E flat.
173.ch: American Brass Band and early bands
173.q: Well, very seldom. E flat cornet is more louder. You understand? They use that more in brass bands that you want to hear it. Now, as a rule, they take an E flat cornet and put that in a concert band. You can hear that damn cornet above all of them. Yeah. It's got a louder tone. But as a rule, we…

181.s: Parker says bands went out with nine or ten men; he played in seven or eight-piece bands.
181.ch: Church funerals, band size and mourning
181.q: Small? Oh, I played in the smallest, seven, eight pieces.

33.t: The eight-piece society orchestra and its instrumentation
33.s: DeDroit gives the makeup of his society orchestra and when he enlarged it, praising trumpeter Al Hurt but noting he was too loud for carnival balls.
33.q: Bass drums, bass drums and piano. First and third alto and second tenor. Now sometimes if I could play for private, you see the country club, they were used to having eight men and they didn't want to spend, you know, they had so much to spend.

624.t: Brass band lineup and whether they read music
624.s: Brunies and Allen list the instruments in the brass bands and say that Fisher and Laine's players mostly did not read music.
624.ch: Playing in clubs and Mardi Gras
624.q: And Abby and Abby. Yeah, Abby was at the Cadillac. Later, the silver slipper of the... Silver slipper, too. I was going to ask one more question about the brass bands. What the lineup was. Like you say, sometime you were the only carnet. How many trombones? What else did they have? Altos,…

40.t: Varying band size and which instrument they miss
40.s: The band can shrink to four or six pieces or drop an instrument; Zanco misses banjo and trombone most. Conner mentions Buddy Bolden's two clarinets.
40.q: Sometimes, yeah. Well, uh, you take some of these, uh, patio parties we might play. They might want more of a, you know, a quiet and down music. So we, uh, we'll mute the trumpet, use a clarinet, piano, drums. Sometimes we'll operate with four pieces, sometimes five, sometimes six, sometimes a full…

601.t: The Pacific Brass Band: size, instruments, leader and Georgia Hooker
601.s: Martin and Russell work out the Pacific band's instrumentation and that it dates back to the 1880s and the Spanish-American War, not to the railroad. Its leader was Joel Lizard, and they talk about the trumpeter Georgia Hooker.
601.ch: Eddie Vinson and the Pacific Brass Band
601.q: No. That band there, that band was up in the 80s. Pacific Band, cause them long, we were Spanish and American War. Yeah, that's right. Back there. Yeah, that's right. See, back there in 1895, all them people was playing-

272.t: The Standard Oil big band and its photographs
272.s: He was hired because of his clarinet and read only when he wanted; the interviewer counts instruments in two big-band photos.
272.ch: Baton Rouge big band and New York
272.q: Oh yes it was a big band. Well I read when I wanted to have a different one I did. In other words I was my own boss. I just told you I want to go to old man Weller. Weller? Weller? Weller here every time he come back he likes old man bringing his kid toys and say he'd bring me more dirt and poofy.…

274.t: Instrumentation of his father's Promo brass band
274.s: Labat lists the pieces in the Promo society brass band: trumpets, baritone, bass, drums, trombones; no clarinet.
274.ch: Bay St. Louis roots and early music

648.t: Instrumentation of the real Dixieland combination
648.s: The five or six-piece combination of cornet, trombone, clarinet, bass, guitar and drums; piano came later up north.
648.q: What instruments were those in the Dixieland? The main instruments, the main five instruments were cornet, trombone, cornet, drums, and we didn't have piano in those days. We had guitar. A great many guitar players played a twelve string guitar to give enough body and rhythm to be heard. In so many…

643.t: Band instrumentation: altos, trombones, E-flat trumpet, Sammy Robins
643.s: They tally the instruments, two altos including Ernest Martin, two trombones, clarinets, no saxophones, an E-flat horn, and trumpeter Sammy Robins.
643.q: Yeah we had two alto I don't forgot the other alto player He's from John He wrote St Charles You got the Martin You could take Ernest Martin We used to play alto too Ernest Martin We were the leader of the band at that time

138.t: Instrumentation of the boys' band, no titles, all white
138.s: The first band had piccolo, clarinet, trombone, cornet, alto, tuba, baritone and drums, made up tunes with no names, and was all white; Laine knows of no earlier ragtime band.
138.q: One piccolo player. And we had clarinet. Clarinet. Trombone. Trombone. Carnet. Alto. Tuba. Tuba. And baritone. Of course, drums, of course. And one piccolo.

295.t: Size of marching and dance bands, and what counts as a jazz band
295.s: Marching bands ran 12-18 men; dance bands were six or seven pieces, and a jazz band was typically seven; violins were dropped for wind instruments before the war.
295.q: It all depend on, uh, the, all depend on what, the, the people wanted. If they wanted six men, well, I'd point at them six men. In them days, we used to call it six men, seven pieces, because the trap drums was in there. See? I see. Uh, did the violin ever play with you, Jack? Yes,

909.t: Henry Allen's band and brass band instrumentation
909.s: Morris played plenty in Henry Allen's Algiers band; the group describes its size, no saxophones, the tenor horn, piccolo and flute.
909.q: You know, he used to play with us. He was in short pants then. Yeah, Henry Allen. And he kept that band for years and years.

198.s: Bands worked every night, usually five pieces, sometimes three, with piano, drums, clarinet, trumpet, trombone, guitar or violin.
198.q: What instruments? Well, I would have the cabra piano, and carolets, trumpets, trombone. Some would have this bass guitar and violin. Some would just have maybe this piano drumming, clarolets. Or maybe trumpet. You know what I'm saying? Three piece. Some would have this piano.

248.s: The O'Neil Lavish band at Puclos was a small group of five: violin, piano, tenor banjo, saxophone and trumpet.
248.q: The O'Neil Lavish here, a violin player. And, let's see. And what did you play, by the way? I was playing the tenor banjo. Tenor banjo.

302.s: The twelve-piece band had three trumpets, three saxes, two trombones, bass horn and piano; comedians doubled on bass drum.
302.ch: Minstrel show life and Ida Cox
302.q: We had three trumpets at one time. They had three saxophones and of course a couple of them double clarinet, the bass horn, two trombones. Then I played the traps, see, for sure I had to play the traps. The bass drummer mostly would be one of the comedians or something like that.

177.t: Joe Gabriel's orchestra and brass band
177.s: Gabriel led an orchestra and a ten-piece brass band, and Jiles describes the instrumentation.
177.q: Yeah. His band carried about seven pieces. The brass band? No, the brass band carried ten pieces. Ten pieces. That's right.

128.t: Repertoire and instrumentation of the country brass band
128.s: The bands played marches, one-steps and quick steps; a band of 13-14 had tenors, altos, E-flat clarinets, one valve trombone, four cornets, tuba and two drums.
128.q: One step, quick step, they were playing all different kinds of music. They didn't fool no, like that, like simple opera music, they didn't fool with that on the time. No, none of the classical.

905.s: Seven-piece band with trumpet, trombone, clarinet, drums, guitar, and Phillips on bass violin.
905.ch: Country years in St. John Parish
905.q: Well, they had a fella they called Fernand Alexander. That was the trumpet player. And the other boy, the trombone player, and the name's No-No Lagrange. No-No Lagrange.

308.t: Sam Morgan band lineup and how bands sat on the stand
308.s: He lists the band's players and shows the single-row seating of six-piece bands, with no piano except on records.
308.ch: Sam Morgan and the Morgan bands
308.q: I'll give you the band over there, the band I'm speaking about during them days was I line them up like how we used to line them up. First come the drum in a row, then come the trombone, Yank on trombone, Alfred Williams on drums, Yank on trombone, Sam Morgan on trumpet, then come Zeb clarinet,…

544.t: Why a nonet: origins and instrumentation
544.s: The nonet grew from a ten-piece band he and Sam DeAngelo formed in Youngstown in summer 1974, and he reworked its book for six horns and three rhythm.
544.q: Well Sam DeAngelo and I had done a band of that size when we were in Youngstown, we did, I used to go back home during the summer to work in factories and whatever, making some money for college. And also, so the summer of 1974 which was just before my senior year in college we decided to put this…

558.t: Septet versus conjunto and Arsenio Rodriguez
558.s: He explains the instrumentation of a septet versus a conjunto and credits Arsenio Rodriguez with creating the conjunto around 1934.
558.q: Well, the septet consists of seven, which are the tres, the guitar, the bass, bongos, trumpet, maracas, and clave - that's the septet. Apart from those instruments I just mentioned, the conjunto has an additional trumpet, piano, and conga. That's the difference.

137.t: Setting the circus band up as an orchestra
137.s: He explains trombones in early jazz, his use of bass drum and trap drummers, French horns for piano sound and clarinets for reeds, and the band's size.
137.ch: Circus shows and learning to voice
137.q: They was sort of voiced with the trumpets. When the trumpets got a little bit too swift, the trombones would (unintelligible) or something else to do, tailgate, they called it.

1.t: Why the old brass bands used no piano
1.s: Bands used bass, guitar, banjo and drum, with trombone, clarinet and cornet in set roles, as with Kid Ory and Preston Jackson.
1.ch: Wagon bands, halls and the old brass bands
1.q: On the wagon... But I mean, the bands, as a rule, never used a piano, because it just was a good sounding thing. A bass, a good guitar and a banjo and a drum, with a good-sized drum that had a boom to it, which was tuned. And it was a sound that was fascinating, because you had the (?) marching, a…

9.t: Boston band instrumentation and the union hangout
9.s: Boston had good reeds, pianos and drummers but scarce brass; musicians hung out in a small union room to find gigs.
9.ch: Boston childhood, learning music and first gigs
9.q: They had brass. They had a trumpet when they could find one. Brass was not plentiful. Good trumpet players were not plentiful up there. Good brass was not plentiful.

409.t: The band grows and starts playing theaters
409.s: By 1931-32 the band was growing into sections and began playing theaters; there were three trumpets.
409.q: Yeah. Because I think we started to going out doing theaters.

379.t: Machito band instrumentation and adding the conga
379.s: He explains starting with two trumpets and saxes, then three trumpets, extra sax and conga.
379.q: Well, I tell you what the sound -- the band started -- I start the band with two trumpets. I can put a whole lot of musicians, but I was afraid nobody was going to pay. The average band in those days was one trumpet and maybe one violin and marimba, all kind of stuff like that, you know. RUMBA

453.t: Instrumentation and swing of the Bernie Young band
453.s: A twelve-piece unit with three brass, three reeds and four rhythm, the same as Armstrong's 1931 band, which he says swung.
453.q: One, two, three -- three brass, three reeds, alto, alto, tenor -- that's right, three brass, three reeds, piano, bass, drums, and let me see -- did we have -- and guitar -- and banjo. Piano, bass drums and banjo.

387.s: The band's instrumentation and working as a committee to get out of block writing.
387.q: We could have gone into strings and french horns, but that was a little much, we thought. It was gilding a lily, because there was the bother of if not directly, then eventually of transporting those things. I don't know how it would have been if we had gone the other way, but this is the way we…
